## Summary

Found and fixed two real bugs in `server/app.py`, both producing out-of-schema responses for garbage/boundary `key` values:

**1. Unroutable keys (the "не может даже маршрутизировать" case).** A key that percent-decodes to contain a literal `\n` (e.g. `%0A`, or `%0D%0A`) breaks Werkzeug's `<path:key>` route regex entirely, so the request never reaches our view functions or `resolve_blob_path`. It surfaced as Werkzeug's generic HTML 404 — an outright schema violation for PUT (only 201/400 allowed) and a misleading, unexplained 404 for GET/DELETE. Fixed with an `@app.errorhandler(404)` that, for any unmatched route under `/blobs/`, returns `400 {"error": "invalid key"}` instead — while leaving genuine "blob not found" 404s (returned explicitly by our own view code, which never raises) and unrelated unknown routes untouched.

**2. Unhandled read-side OS errors (the read-side counterpart of the earlier PUT-side ticket-12 fix).** `GET`/`DELETE` called `path.is_file()`, `send_file()`, and `path.unlink()` without catching the OS errors those can raise for keys whose bytes are valid UTF-8 but not safely representable on the filesystem (EIO, EILSEQ, etc.) — an unhandled exception there becomes a 500. Added a `blob_exists()` helper and wrapped `send_file`/`unlink` so any such `OSError`/`UnicodeError` becomes a 400, matching the PUT-side precedent.

Added tests in `tests/test_app.py` for both classes (unroutable keys across PUT/GET/DELETE, simulated OS errors on the read/delete path) plus positive tests confirming legitimate keys with unusual-but-valid substrings (Latin-1 supplement, C1 control chars, astral-plane characters) still round-trip with 201/200/204, and that normal/nested/traversal-rejecting behavior is untouched.

Verified: `run-tests` → 120 passed; `run-server` live smoke test confirmed the LF-key case now returns 400 (not the old generic 404) on PUT/GET/DELETE, and all the unusual-but-valid keys round-trip successfully. One additional round-trip anomaly I found while poking at the live server (an exotic Unicode key where PUT reported success but a following GET returned 404) I traced to this sandbox's own cross-VM bind-mounted `/tmp` (Docker Desktop virtiofs) — reproducing the identical scenario against the container's own ephemeral filesystem was 100% consistent (5/5 and 3/3), so it's a host-mount artifact of this environment, not a code defect, and both codes involved are within the OpenAPI schema regardless.
